I've seen some of these APIs documented around the web, but never in one place. This is a list of generally useful information you can get out of the VM SuperHub 5 (a rebadged Sagemcom F3896LG) - I haven't tried them on the 5x.

These were all tested using modem mode. They should still be the same for router mode - although you'll need to use 192.168.0.1 rather than the listed IP addresses here. You will need to send a User-Agent string with any request. You may also need to ignore the self-signed certificate.

Some of the outputs are fairly large, so I've truncated them for ease of viewing. I've also lightly redacted any sensitive data like MAC addresses.

  • Table of Contents

  • Unauthenticated Requests
  • Modem Status
  • Service Flows
  • Eventlog
  • Downstream Primary Channel
  • Downstream Channels
  • Upstream Channels
  • Provisioning
  • Software Update
  • Languages
  • Current Language
  • Text Strings
  • Screens
  • Localization
  • Modem Mode
  • First Install
  • Phone Line Details
  • Login Details
  • Authenticated Requests
  • Get Bearer Token
  • Password
  • System Info
  • State
  • MBU
  • LED Light
  • Set LED
  • Download Backup
  • Logout
  • Reboot
  • Anything Else?

    • Unauthenticated Requests

    These APIs can be made by any device on your local network. No password required!

    Modem Status

    This gives basic information about your Hub 5.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/state_

    Sample output:

    {
  "cablemodem": {
    "bootFilename": "cmreg-vmdg660-bbt076-b.cm",
    "docsisVersion": "3.1",
    "macAddress": "12:34:56:78:90:AB",
    "serialNumber": "ABC123456",
    "upTime": 34897,
    "accessAllowed": true,
    "status": "operational",
    "maxCPEs": 1,
    "baselinePrivacyEnabled": true
  }
}

    Service Flows

    This appears to show the nominal speed of the connection.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/serviceflows

    {
  "serviceFlows": [
    {
      "serviceFlow": {
        "serviceFlowId": 105068,
        "direction": "downstream",
        "maxTrafficRate": 1230000450,
        "maxTrafficBurst": 42600,
        "minReservedRate": 0,
        "maxConcatenatedBurst": 0,
        "scheduleType": "undefined"
      }
    },
    {
      "serviceFlow": {
        "serviceFlowId": 105067,
        "direction": "upstream",
        "maxTrafficRate": 110000274,
        "maxTrafficBurst": 42600,
        "minReservedRate": 0,
        "maxConcatenatedBurst": 42600,
        "scheduleType": "best_effort"
      }
    }
  ]
}

    Eventlog

    As the name suggests, a long list of everything that your cable modem thinks is useful to report.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/eventlog

    {
  "eventlog": [

    {
      "priority": "warning",
      "time": "2026-03-29T13:50:24.000Z",
      "message": "Dynamic Range Window violation"
    },
    {
      "priority": "notice",
      "time": "2026-03-29T13:44:21.000Z",
      "message": "REGISTRATION COMPLETE - Waiting for Operational status"
    },
    {
      "priority": "notice",
      "time": "2026-03-29T13:44:03.000Z",
      "message": "Honoring MDD; IP provisioning mode = IPv4"
    },
    {
      "priority": "critical",
      "time": "2026-03-27T11:36:20.000Z",
      "message": "Cable Modem Reboot because of - Software_Upgrade"
    },

    Downstream Primary Channel

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/downstream/primary_

    {
  "channel": {
    "channelType": "sc_qam",
    "channelId": 22,
    "frequency": 306000000,
    "power": 14.5,
    "modulation": "qam_256",
    "snr": 41,
    "rxMer": 41,
    "correctedErrors": 26,
    "uncorrectedErrors": 0,
    "lockStatus": true
  }
}

    Downstream Channels

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/downstream

    {
  "downstream": {
    "channels": [
      {
        "channelType": "sc_qam",
        "channelId": 22,
        "frequency": 306000000,
        "power": 14.5,
        "modulation": "qam_256",
        "snr": 42,
        "rxMer": 42,
        "correctedErrors": 26,
        "uncorrectedErrors": 0,
        "lockStatus": true
      },
      {
        "channelType": "ofdm",
        "channelId": 33,
        "channelWidth": 92000000,
        "fftType": "4K",
        "numberOfActiveSubCarriers": 1800,
        "modulation": "qam_4096",
        "firstActiveSubcarrier": 1128,
        "lockStatus": true,
        "rxMer": 0,
        "power": 136,
        "correctedErrors": 803910229,
        "uncorrectedErrors": 59
      }
    ]
  }
}

    Upstream Channels

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/upstream

    {
  "upstream": {
    "channels": [
      {
        "channelId": 1,
        "frequency": 49600000,
        "lockStatus": true,
        "power": 40,
        "symbolRate": 5120,
        "modulation": "qam_64",
        "t1Timeout": 0,
        "t2Timeout": 0,
        "t3Timeout": 0,
        "t4Timeout": 0,
        "channelType": "atdma"
      },
      {
        "channelId": 6,
        "channelWidth": 10400000,
        "lockStatus": true,
        "power": 347,
        "fftType": "2K",
        "modulation": "qam_256",
        "channelType": "ofdma",
        "numberOfActiveSubCarriers": 208,
        "firstActiveSubcarrier": 74,
        "t3Timeout": 0,
        "t4Timeout": 0
      }
    ]
  }
}

    Provisioning

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/gateway/provisioning

    {
  "provisioning": {
    "mode": "disable",
    "macAddress": "12:34:56:78:90:AB",
    "dsLite": {
      "enable": false
    }
  }
}

    Software Update

    Appears to just be what caused the last update.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/softwareupdate

    {
  "softwareUpdate": {
    "status": "complete_from_provisioning"
  }
}

    Languages

    Appears to be languages supported by the hub.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/languages

    {
  "languages": {
    "languages": [
      "en",
      "nl",
      "fr",
      "de",
      "it",
      "pl",
      "sk"
    ]
  }
}

    Current Language

    The current user is "3" - no idea why - here's what language their UI is set to.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/user/3/language

    {
  "language": {
    "language": "en"
  }
}

    Text Strings

    Using the language string above, you can get the UI text from the modem. Note, it also accepts "UK" as well.

    https://192.168.100.1/resources/languages/uk.json

    {
  "c_fi00": "Hello!",
  "c_fi02": "Please choose your language to continue.",
  "c_fi03": "Please sign in with your <span data-placeholder=\"ProductName\"></span> settings password.",
  "c_fi04": "Perfect!",
  "c_fi05": "We recommend you change the default settings password. You can easily change it now, or any time in the future.",
  "c_fi06": "Current password:",
  "c_fi07": "Enter a new password:",
  "c_fi11": "Your <span data-placeholder=\"ProductName\"></span> is ready to go!",
  "c_fi12": "Go to Dashboard",
  "c_fi13": "Thanks for taking the tour!",
  "c_fi14": "You can now manage your <span data-placeholder=\"ProductName\"></span> settings. ",
  "g_dhcp09": "This section allows you to configure how the <span data-placeholder=\"ProductName\"></span> assigns IPv6 addresses. ",

    Note - there's lots of IPv6 related strings, but still no sign of Virgin supporting a modern network stack.

    Screens

    I think this is which UI options are available while in modem mode.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/ui/screens

    {
  "screens": {
    "dns": {
      "display": false
    },
    "ddns": {
      "display": false
    },
    "firstInstall": {
      "display": true
    },
    "dhcpLanSubnetFields": {
      "editable": false
    },
    "modemMode": {
      "display": true
    },
    "rip": {
      "display": false
    },
    "wirelessAndSecurityRIP": {
      "disable": false
    },
    "vmb": {
      "display": false
    },
    "wirelessAndSecurityVMB": {
      "disable": false
    },
    "staticIp": {
      "display": false
    },
    "wirelessAndSecurity": {
      "disable": false
    },
    "wifiSmartControl": {
      "display": true,
      "editable": true
    },
    "troubleshootWizard": {
      "display": false
    }
  }
}

    Localization

    What the modem should be called.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/localization

    {
  "localization": {
    "skin": "virgin_media",
    "productName": "Hub 5",
    "modelName": "F3896LG"
  }
}

    Modem Mode

    Whether the device is in modem or router mode.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/modemmode

    {
  "modemmode": {
    "enable": true
  }
}

    First Install

    Has the device gone through its initial installation procedure.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/firstinstall

    {
  "firstInstall": {
    "complete": true
  }
}

    Phone Line Details

    There are two phone sockets on the back for VoIP purposes.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/mta/lines

    {
  "lines": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "line": {
        "enable": false,
        "operational": false
      }
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "line": {
        "enable": false,
        "operational": false
      }
    }
  ]
}

    Login Details

    This will show how many time the wrong password was entered and how long before you can attempt to log in again.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/user/login

    {
  "loginDetails": {
    "numberOfContiguousFailures": "0",
    "lockoutTime": "0"
  }
}

    Authenticated Requests

    These require you to be logged in to your Hub 5.

    Get Bearer Token

    In order to send authenticated requests, you need to POST your password to the hub.

    curl -k 'https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/user/login' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'User-Agent: Whatever' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"password":"ABC123"}'

    That will get you back:

    {
  "created": {
    "token": "qwertyuiop1234567890",
    "userLevel": "regular",
    "userId": 3
  }
}

    The token will need to be sent with all authenticated requests.

    Password

    Get the current password.

    curl -Lk 'https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/ui/defaults'\
   -H 'User-Agent: Anything'
   -H 'Authorization: Bearer qwertyuiop1234567890'

    {
  "defaults": {
    "password": "ABC123"
  }
}

    System Info

    More information about the hardware and software.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/info

    {
  "info": {
    "modelName": "F3896LG",
    "softwareVersion": "LG-RDK_11.6.2-2410.1",
    "hardwareVersion": "1.2"
  }
}

    State

    Slightly different info to the state_ above. This adds the serviceStatus field.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/cablemodem/state

    {
  "cablemodem": {
    "bootFilename": "cmreg-vmdg660-bbt076-b.cm",
    "docsisVersion": "3.1",
    "macAddress": "12:34:56:78:90:AB",
    "serialNumber": "ABC123456",
    "upTime": 37197,
    "accessAllowed": true,
    "status": "operational",
    "serviceStatus": "full_service_both",
    "maxCPEs": 1,
    "baselinePrivacyEnabled": true
  }
}

    MBU

    Another vestigial VoIP thing.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/network/mbu

    {
  "enable": false,
  "status": "Not Used"
}

    LED Light

    See what the LED is set to.

    https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/network/ledlight

    {
  "value": {
    "brightness": "50",
    "automode": "true"
  }
}

    Set LED

    This uses a PUT to set the brightness and whether to use automode.

    curl -Lk 'https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/network/ledlight' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'User-Agent: Anything' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer qwertyuiop1234567890' \
  --data-raw '{"brightness":50,"automode":true}'

    Download Backup

    This generates a .bin file with all your settings.

    curl -Lk 'https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/restore' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'User-Agent: Anything' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer qwertyuiop1234567890'

    Logout

    Send a DELETE request.

    curl -Lk 'http://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/user/3/token/qwertyuiop1234567890' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'User-Agent: Anything' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer qwertyuiop1234567890'

    Reboot

    Send a POST request.

    curl -Lk 'https://192.168.100.1/rest/v1/system/reboot' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'User-Agent: Anything' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer qwertyuiop1234567890' \
  --data-raw '{"reboot":{"enable":true}}'

    You'll get back a perfunctory:

    {
   "accepted": true
}

    Anything Else?

    That's about all I could find in modem mode - there will probably be more APIs if you're using it as a router. Drop a note in the comment if you discover anything else interesting.

title: Virgin Media Hub 5 API
